Founded on 24 October 1946, FK Sarajevo was the most successful club from [[SR Bosnia and Herzegovina]] in [[SFR Yugoslavia|Yugoslavia]], winning two [[Yugoslav First League]] titles, finishing runners-up on two other occasions, reaching the [[Yugoslav Cup]] final twice and placing 6th in the Yugoslav First League [[Yugoslav First League#All-Time First Yugoslav League Table|all-time table]].{{cite web|url=http://strategija.org/vecna-lista-fudbalskih-prvenstava-sfr-jugoslavije/|title=Večna lista fudbalskih prvenstava SFR Jugoslavije|date=3 February 2013 |publisher=Strategija.org|access-date=17 March 2014|archive-date=23 February 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140223111317/http://strategija.org/vecna-lista-fudbalskih-prvenstava-sfr-jugoslavije/|url-status=live}} Today, FK Sarajevo is one of the most prominent members of the [[Premier League of Bosnia and Herzegovina]], where it has won five [[Premier League of Bosnia and Herzegovina|Bosnian championships]], eight [[Bosnia and Herzegovina Football Cup|Bosnian Cups]] and one [[Bosnian Supercup]]. Furthermore, the club finished runners-up in the national championship another seven times. It is ranked second in the Premier League of Bosnia and Herzegovina all-time table. FK Sarajevo is the most popular football club in the country, alongside [[FK Željezničar Sarajevo|FK Željezničar]], with whom it shares a fierce rivalry in the [[Sarajevo derby]], often called the ''Eternal derby'' ([[Bosnian language|Bosnian]]: Vječiti derbi).{{cite web |title=Sarajevo stage set for unique eternal derby |url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/0203-0f8821514c79-9b933c0b69c1-1000--sarajevo-stage-set-for-unique-eternal-derby/ |website=UEFA.com |date=2 November 2012 |access-date=15 June 2025}} This fixture is not only Bosnia and Herzegovina's premier football rivalry, but it has also been recognized internationally, being featured among [[FourFourTwo]]’s ''50 Biggest Derbies in the World''.{{cite web |title=FourFourTwo's 50 Biggest Derbies in the World |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/fourfourtwos-50-biggest-derbies-world |website=FourFourTwo |date= 25 April 2016|access-date=15 June 2025}} The club plays its home matches at the [[Asim Ferhatović Hase Stadium]], also known as the Koševo Stadium, named after legendary club striker [[Asim Ferhatović]], and located in the city's [[Koševo]] neighborhood. The stadium has a current capacity of 34,700 and is the largest in the country.{{cite web|url=http://www.worldstadiums.com/europe/countries/bosnia_herzegovina.shtml|title=World Stadiums – Stadiums in Bosnia & Herzegovina|work=worldstadiums.com|access-date=27 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170501131039/http://www.worldstadiums.com/europe/countries/bosnia_herzegovina.shtml|archive-date=1 May 2017|url-status=dead}} FK Sarajevo also operates the [[Butmir Training Centre]] in the [[Ilidža]] municipality, a state-of-the-art facility spanning 70,000 m² and opened in 2015. The centre includes multiple FIFA-standard pitches, modern fitness and rehabilitation infrastructure, and serves as the training base for the men’s, women’s, youth teams and [[FK Sarajevo B|Sarajevo B]].{{cite web|url=https://fksarajevo.ba/bs/novost/akademija-fk-sarajevo-razvija-vrhunske-sportske-talente-u-trening-centru-butmir/7607|title=Akademija FK Sarajevo razvija vrhunske sportske talente u Trening centru Butmir|date=15 May 2023|access-date=15 June 2025|language=bs|author=|publisher=fksarajevo.ba}}{{cite web|url=https://www.klix.ba/sport/nogomet/mirvic-se-pohvalio-zavrsenim-prvim-dijelom-radova-u-butmiru/240229084|title=Mirvić se pohvalio završenim prvim dijelom radova u Butmiru|date=29 February 2024|access-date=15 June 2025|language=bs|author=|publisher=Klix.ba}} The traditional colours of the club are [[maroon]] and white, with the home kit traditionally consisting of a maroon shirt, white shorts, and maroon socks - a combination that has become one of the most iconic and recognizable in Yugoslav and Bosnian sports.{{cite web|url=https://fk-sarajevo.ba/bs/klub/grb-i-boje/2|title=Grb i boje|date=15 June 2025|access-date=15 June 2025|language=bs|author=|publisher=fk-sarajevo.ba}} The club’s historic nickname is the Maroon-Whites ([[Bosnian language|Bosnian]]: Bordo-bijeli), in reference to its traditional maroon and white colours. Over the decades, the club has also been affectionately known as the Sarajevan Aghas ([[Bosnian language|Bosnian]]: Age Sarajlije), a nickname that alludes both to the [[Ottoman Bosnia and Herzegovina|Ottoman-era]] [[aghas]] and to a well-known [[sevdalinka]], "[[Vino piju nane age Sarajlije]]", which nostalgically evokes the city’s cultural identity. In recent years, another popular nickname has emerged: The Giants ([[Bosnian language|Bosnian]]: Divovi), inspired by [[Benjamin Isović]]’s football ballad, "[[Mi smo divovi]]" ([[English language|English]]: We Are Giants), which subsequently became the club’s official anthem.{{cite web|url=https://radiosarajevo.ba/sport/nogomet/benjamin-isovic-mi-smo-divovi-je-vise-od-navijacke-pjesme/237382|title=Benjamin Isović: 'Mi smo divovi' je više od navijačke pjesme|date=28 April 2016|access-date=15 June 2025|language=bs|author=|publisher=radiosarajevo.ba}} In addition to its domestic achievements, FK Sarajevo is widely regarded as the most significant exporter of footballing talent in Bosnia and Herzegovina.{{cite web |title=Oboren rekord izlaznog transfera u BiH: Čelik prodan za 2,5 miliona eura |url=https://www.jabuka.tv/oboren-rekord-izlaznog-transfera-u-bih/ |website=Jabuka.tv |date=6 February 2024 |access-date=13 June 2025}} The club holds seven out of the ten highest player transfer fees in the history of Bosnian football, underlining its role as an incubator of talent for European leagues.{{cite web |title=Milioneri sa Koševa: FK Sarajevo u posljednjih pet sezona od transfera zaradio više od 8 miliona eura |url=https://www.klix.ba/sport/nogomet/milioneri-sa-koseva-fk-sarajevo-u-posljednjih-pet-sezona-od-transfera-zaradio-vise-od-8-miliona-eura/240729135 |website=Klix.ba |date=29 July 2024 |access-date=13 June 2025}} The club’s success in the transfer market is largely attributed to its renowned [[FK Sarajevo Youth School|youth academy]], which has consistently produced top-tier talent for both domestic competitions and European clubs.{{cite web |title=Milioneri sa Koševa: FK Sarajevo u posljednjih pet sezona od transfera zaradio više od 8 miliona eura |url=https://www.klix.ba/sport/nogomet/milioneri-sa-koseva-fk-sarajevo-u-posljednjih-pet-sezona-od-transfera-zaradio-vise-od-8-miliona-eura/240729135 |website=Klix.ba |date=29 July 2024 |access-date=13 June 2025}} Beyond its sporting achievements, FK Sarajevo holds a significant role in the social and cultural landscape of the capital. The club reflects Sarajevo’s [[multicultural]] character and has a broad support base representing diverse communities within the city, country and the wider region.{{cite web |title=FK Sarajevo: A Symbol of Sarajevo's Multicultural Identity |url=https://www.footballhistory.org/club/sarajevo.html |website=FootballHistory.org |access-date=15 June 2025}}{{cite web |title=From the war to Vincent Tan: the history that shaped FK Sarajevo |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2019/jul/09/fk-sarajevo-champions-league-qualifier-war-vincent-tan |website=The Guardian |date=9 July 2019 |access-date=15 June 2025}}{{cite web |title=Celtic come from behind to beat Sarajevo in first leg of Champions League qualifier |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2019/07/09/celtic-come-behind-beat-saravejo-first-leg-champions-league/ |website=The Telegraph |date=9 July 2019 |access-date=15 June 2025}}"}}
